title: Easing workbench
description: Two editable curve handles connect time to a moving white marker on a cobalt timing instrument.
useCase: Authoring and inspecting CSS timing curves with a synchronized, seekable motion preview.
interaction: Drag the handles, scrub time, play the motion, or copy the CSS curve
reducedMotion: Playback becomes explicit quarter-step advancement; manual scrubbing and curve editing remain available.
limitations: Both control-point coordinates are bounded to 0–1. It covers CSS cubic timing curves without overshoot; not a spring simulator.
look: Cobalt-blue panel with a white bezier curve on a faint grid, hollow white handles, a side track with a large white marker and monospace controls.
motion: Play runs time linearly over the duration (1200 ms default) while a bead rides the curve and a side marker tracks the eased value; handle drags reshape it live.
adapt: `valueAtTime` solves the curve by bisection on x and `screenPoint` maps 0–1 values into the graph; `tick` advances `progressRef` by elapsed time over `duration`. Change the `START` handles and feed `curve` (the CSS string) to your own animation.
